transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise

That can be worrying, but 'horrible noise' covers a few different issues. To figure out what's going on safely, I need to know exactly when it happens and what it sounds like. Could you describe the noise (e.g. grinding, rattling, screeching) and tell me when it happens? Is it during the wash cycle, only when draining water, or specifically during the spin/drying phase?
[Helpful to see: image "Check the transit bolts have been removed" — Transit bolts hold the drum still for delivery and must be removed before use — a machine that bangs, walks or vibrates (especially when new or recently moved) often still has them fitted. They unscrew from the back of the machine. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
It's a loud roaring rumble when it spins, like a jet engine. A little noisy during the wash but much worse on spin. Been getting worse over a couple of months.

[Heading: Likely worn drum bearings]
A loud roaring rumble that gets worse as the spin speed increases is classic for worn drum bearings. This usually happens gradually over months or years as the grease inside the bearing fails. To confirm this safely, please unplug the machine first. Open the door and try to wiggle the metal inner drum up and down firmly with your hand (push down on one side of the rim, then lift up). Does it feel loose with a clunking play, or is it firm? Also, spin the drum by hand: does it rotate smoothly or do you hear/feel any grinding? If there is significant play or roughness, the bearings (and likely the spider arm they sit on) need replacing. This is a major repair involving full disassembly of the machine.
Ok did that with it off. The drum rumbles and grinds when I turn it, and there's a clunky up and down play when I lift the edge. Is it worth fixing? It was about £350 new, 9 years old.

[Heading: Failed drum bearings and likely spider arm]
The clunky play and grinding confirm that the drum bearings have failed. Given it’s 9 years old and was £350 new, I’d strongly advise against repairing it. The labour involved in replacing bearings (and likely the spider arm they sit on) usually costs more than a new machine, and at this age other components like the motor or electronics are also nearing the end of their life. It’s time to replace the appliance.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok, the model on the door label is ZWF81443W

[Heading: Failed drum bearings]
Thanks for providing the model number. As we established, the clunky play and grinding confirm that the drum bearings have failed. Given it’s 9 years old and was £350 new, I’d strongly advise against repairing it. It’s time to replace the appliance.
